title: Vivekanand Business School Takes 180 Management Students on Global Industry Immersion Programme in Thailand
summary: Vivekanand Business School, Mumbai, took 180 management students to Thailand for a five-day programme of visits to Electrolux, Toyota, Yakult and Ichitan and a workshop at Bangkok University.
body_html:
Mumbai, 2 November 2026: Vivekanand Business School (VBS) organised a five-day Global Industry Immersion Programme in Thailand for 180 management students from different specialisations. The programme combined industry visits, academic interactions and cultural experiences, with the aim of linking classroom learning to practical business applications and giving students a first-hand view of international business practices and global industry operations.

During the programme, students visited the facilities of Electrolux, Toyota, Yakult and Ichitan, where they studied global manufacturing practices, operational efficiency, quality management and sustainability in a real-world setting.

At Electrolux, the students explored lean inventory management and sustainable engineering. At Toyota, they learnt about the Toyota Production System and Just-in-Time inventory management. The visit to Yakult focused on quality control and hygiene standards, while at Ichitan the group observed automated production and eco-friendly packaging.

Alongside the industry visits, the students attended a workshop on teaching and learning methodologies at Bangkok University. The session offered them international academic exposure and helped strengthen their understanding of cross-cultural collaboration and global business practices.

Speaking about the programme, Sandeep Bhardwaj, Director, Vivekanand Business School, said, “Management education must go beyond classroom learning to help students understand how businesses operate in different markets and cultural environments. This international immersion programme provided students with an opportunity to observe global industry practices, understand operational challenges and engage with diverse perspectives. Such experiences are important in developing the critical thinking, adaptability and problem-solving skills required of future business leaders.”

The school said the Global Industry Immersion Programme is part of its wider emphasis on experiential learning as an integral part of management education. By connecting management concepts with industry practice and international exposure, VBS aims to prepare its students to navigate changing business environments and respond effectively to the needs of industry and society.
